transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2027-02-09 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Meyers (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Marco Alvarez (Redwood SE), Samantha Liu (HelioCloud PM), Arjun Rao (HelioCloud Cloud Eng), Lena Park (HelioCloud Security)

[00:00] Jordan Meyers: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um this is Jordan from Redwood. we have Priya and Marco on the call, and then I see Samantha, Arjun, Lena from HelioCloud. quick round robin?
[00:08] Samantha Liu: hi thanks Jordan, Sam Liu here, partner PM. Arjun and Lena with me. excited to get the integration moving.
[00:12] Priya Singh: hey all, Priya, i'm the systems eng working on the marketplace flow and onboarding.
[00:18] Marco Alvarez: Marco, Solutions Eng. i'll help with reference arch and deployment patterns.
[00:23] Jordan: cool, agenda - marketplace listing steps, reference architecture options (hosted vs private VPC/on-prem), security checklist, test plan, timelines and next steps.
[00:31] Samantha: sounds good. we want to make sure listing goes live by mid march and that our buyers can choose both hosted and private options. budget questions later but first security sign off is must.
[00:41] Jordan: understood. quick qual: do you expect most customers to use Redwood hosted API behind HelioCloud marketplace, or will they prefer a dedicated/reserved Redwood Dedicated or Private deployment?
[00:50] Arjun Rao: good question. helio's enterprise customers often require VPC or private deployment, but we have a fair share of smaller customers that'd prefer hosted. so we need both options listed and clear differences.
[01:03] Priya: ok good - on our side we expose hosted API keys and we can also support marketplace-driven dedicated reservations. for private we have a VPC package and an on-prem appliance variant. there are a couple of networking caveats - e.g. KMS integrations and cross-account peering - we'll document.
[01:20] Lena Park: security - we'll need SOC2 and ISO attestations, certs for data in transit and at rest, KMS/HSM options, audit logs, and SSO/SAML support. also want clarity on data retention and how caches (KV cache) are handled.
[01:33] Marco: yep, we can provide SOC2 reports and ISO outlines; Redwood supports customer-managed KMS via key references and HSM via our private deploy options. KV cache is per-tenant and can be disabled if required - we'll note that in the RA.
[01:48] Jordan: there's sometimes confusion on terms in docs - we call our private option "Redwood Private" and Dedicated is reserved capacity. sometimes transcribed docs use other names - we'll make naming consistent for the listing.
[01:58] Samantha: great. on marketplace listing fields - we need a short description, pricing tiers, deployment options, screenshots, support SLA, and partner contact. we also need co-marketing blurb.
[02:10] Priya: for screenshots pls let us know which flows you want - onboarding, console dashboard (cost/latency breakdown), and reference arch diagrams. we can provide a 1200x600 hero and smaller images.
[02:21] Arjun: for the RA diagram we need explicit VPC peering steps and expected egress flows. also want to understand latency numbers for hosted (p99 and avg tokens) so we can surface in listing.
[02:34] Marco: typical hosted p95 is ~150-220ms for 512 tokens on our verified models, p99 around 350-600ms depending on region and model family. for Dedicated with reserved capacity you'll see much lower tail latency and predictable throughput. i'll share model-specific profiles in the doc.
[02:56] Samantha: ok can you include cost guidance? customers ask about cost per token and what batching savings look like.
[03:04] Priya: yes we'll include estimated unit economics and mention batching/caching benefits. note quantization profiles can reduce cost but there are quality trade-offs - we'll note recommended models for production workloads.
[03:18] Lena: security question - how do you handle audit logs and access control? we need to ensure RBAC maps to our partner provisioning and that logs can be forwarded to our SIEM.
[03:28] Marco: we have token-level audit logs, per-route traces, and can stream logs to customer-managed logging endpoints (S3/Elk/GCS). RBAC integrates with SAML/SSO and we support role mappings. we'll add a sample policy for partner provisioning.
[03:42] Jordan: another operational note - marketplace provisioning flow: when a customer purchases via HelioCloud marketplace, we can auto-provision a trial hosted tenant or kick off a Dedicated reservation workflow. we'll need to wire up webhook calls for provisioning and billing reconciliation.
[03:58] Samantha: yes we need the webhook schema and expected auth. also want a test flow so our QA can exercise provisioning without touching production.
[04:07] Priya: we'll give a sandbox webhook endpoint and a postman collection; SE will set up a test tenant.
[04:14] Arjun: about private deployments - what is the expected onboarding timeline and resource needs (GPU types, disk, network)?
[04:22] Marco: for our on-prem package typical minimum is 8x A100-ish or equivalent for decent throughput; for Redwood Private in a VPC we can run smaller clusters depending on load. onboarding for Private takes ~4-6 weeks end-to-end, Dedicated ~2-3 weeks, hosted is immediate.
[04:39] Samantha: that helps for our marketplace listing to set expectations.
[04:44] Jordan: on integrations, we should finalize two reference architectures: 1) Quickstart hosted via marketplace (auto-provision + API key), 2) Enterprise VPC reference for private deployments (peering, KMS, audit logs). do you want separate RA docs per customer use-case?
[04:59] Samantha: yes two RAs, and a combined joint-solution doc for HelioCloud's SI partners.
[05:06] Priya: noted. we'll draft RA diagrams and a step-by-step checklist.
[05:11] Lena: can we have a security review checklist - who signs off and approximate SLA for security questions?
[05:18] Jordan: typically our security team responds within 5 business days for standard SOC2 questions; for deeper architecture reviews we'll schedule a 1:1 with our security engineering. expect 7-10 business days.
[05:29] Lena: ok please capture that. also we may ask for a pen test report if the customer requires.
[05:34] Marco: we can share high level pen test summaries and process for requesting full reports under NDA.
[05:41] Samantha: great. co-marketing - marketing ops on our side will need a joint blurb and approved logos. can we do a 1 pager for the marketplace tile?
[05:50] Jordan: yes. we'll provide a short marketing one-pager and a co-branded case study template.
[05:55] Samantha: timeline recap - we want draft listing by Feb 12, SE sandbox provision by Feb 16, RA review week of Feb 22, and final listing signoff by March 10. does that timeline work?
[06:07] Priya: seems realistic. I'll aim for provisioning by the 16th.
[06:11] Arjun: QA will need credentials and test data, also synthetic latency tests to validate host performance.
[06:18] Marco: we'll supply synthetic test harness and sample prompts. also include guidance on tokenization differences between models.
[06:28] Jordan: ok i'll send the marketplace onboarding doc and the initial listing draft after this call.
[06:33] Samantha: thanks. action items?
[06:36] Jordan: Action items we captured: Jordan to send pricing and onboarding doc by Feb 12; Priya to provision test tenant by Feb 16; Samantha to share partner assets by Feb 11; Lena to share SOC2/ISO cert timelines by Feb 18.
[06:50] Samantha: that's right. anything else?
[06:53] Lena: small note - please call out the option to disable KV cache per tenant in the RA, we have customers who require no caching.
[07:01] Marco: yes we'll call that out and show config snippet.
[07:06] Jordan: thanks everyone - we'll follow up with the docs and schedule the RA review.
[07:11] Samantha: thanks team. bye.

Notes/Artifacts shared: marketplace_onboarding_draft.docx (link), redwood-ra-hosted-vpc.pdf (link), se-test-collection.postman (link)

End of transcript.
